retention.yaml holds one list, `policies:`. Each policy has `table`, `ttl` and optionally `column`. The write gate (write_file, edit_file, `benmore push`, `benmore deploy`) and `benmore check` refuse any other key in a policy, and any other top-level key except in the file keyed by table name described below. A policy with a key it does not take does not run: a misspelled `column:` is never read as the default column. app.yaml has no `retention:` key.

`table` (required): one of the app's own tables. A `_benmore_*` or `sqlite_*` table is refused and a policy on one never runs: no policy deletes accounts, sessions, jobs or audit rows. A table the app does not have is also refused.

`ttl` (required): how old a row may get, as a quoted string: days ("90d"), years ("1y" is 365 days) or a duration in hours and minutes ("36h", "90m"). Any other value ("2w", a bare 30, "0d") is refused when the file is written and when the app loads, with the same message: `retention.yaml: policy requires table and positive ttl` (api({at:'recovery'}) rejected_reload).

`column` (optional, default `created_at`): the timestamp column the age is measured from. Name another column to expire rows on a date of their own (`expires_at`). A column the table lacks is refused, and the policy does not run at all: it deletes nothing, soft-deleted rows included.

A file keyed by table name (`events: {ttl: 90d, column: created_at}`, or such entries under one `tables:` key) is not a policy list and runs nothing: nothing is deleted for it. It is accepted with a warning that prints the same tables, ttl and column as a `policies:` list to paste in.

An app that was deployed with a policy that does not run keeps loading. Its log names each one at every start as `RETENTION NOT RUNNING`, and an admin's GET /health lists `checks.retention`: `policies_running`, `status` (`ok`, `degraded` when some policies do not run, `not_running` when none does), `not_running` (the reasons) and, when nothing runs, `note: "retention.yaml: no policy is running"` (for a file keyed by table name, `detail` holds the corrected file).
